1.title: Quick-Reference Recap and Service Chooser
1.text: Welcome to Module fifteen: the Quick-Reference Recap and Service Chooser. There are no new topics here. This module puts the whole course on a few pages. You will see look-alike services side by side, a chooser that turns a need into a service, the lists the exam likes, and the terms that trip people up. Use it as your last review before the exam, and come back to it whenever you want a fast refresh.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. See the whole exam on one page: the domains, their weights and where each topic lives. Tell look-alike services apart, in pairs and in sets. Use a need-to-service chooser for the questions that describe a need and ask for the service. And recall the lists the exam likes, together with the terms that trip people up.

1.title: Case Check-In: Tidewater's Final Review
1.text: Tidewater's shop now runs on A W S, with accounts, security, servers, storage, databases, networks and cost controls. Before the exam, the founder wants one page per topic, not fourteen modules. The team keeps mixing up look-alike services, and each mix-up can cost a point. Your job is to review quickly, and to fix the confusions that cost points.

1.title: The Exam on One Page
1.text: Here is the exam on one page. Domain one, Cloud Concepts, is twenty-four percent, and it lives in Modules one and two: the six advantages, elasticity, high availability and cloud economics, then the six pillars, the C A F and the seven Rs. Domain two, Security and Compliance, is thirty percent, in Modules three to five: shared responsibility, Artifact, encryption, CloudTrail, CloudWatch and Config, I A M, and the security services. Domain three, Cloud Technology and Services, is thirty-four percent, in Modules six to twelve. Domain four, Billing, Pricing, and Support, is twelve percent, in Modules thirteen and fourteen. The exam has sixty-five questions, ninety minutes, and you need seven hundred on a scale of one hundred to one thousand. Exam tip: Domains one and two together are more than half of the exam, so do not skip them.

1.title: Look-Alikes: Security and Identity
1.text: First, the security look-alikes. GuardDuty finds threats in logs, Inspector finds vulnerabilities, and Macie finds sensitive data in S three. Detective finds the root cause of a finding, and Security Hub gives one view of findings and standards. W A F filters web requests, Shield stops D D o S attacks, and Firewall Manager applies one policy across many accounts. K M S manages keys, CloudHSM gives dedicated hardware, and Certificate Manager handles certificates. A user has long-term credentials, a group shares permissions, and a role gives temporary credentials. Secrets Manager rotates secrets, and Parameter Store holds plain settings. Identity Center is for your workforce, Cognito is for your app's customers, and Directory Service is for Active Directory. CloudTrail tells you who did it, CloudWatch tells you how healthy it is, and Config tells you what changed. And a security group is stateful and sits at the resource, while a network A C L is stateless and sits at the subnet. Exam tip: learn the one-line job of each, because the exam describes the job, not the name.

1.title: Look-Alikes: Compute, Storage and Databases
1.text: Next, compute, storage and databases. A load balancer shares traffic, and Auto Scaling adds and removes servers. E C S is the A W S way to orchestrate containers, E K S is Kubernetes, and E C R is the library for container images. Fargate runs containers with no servers to manage, and Lambda runs functions when events happen. E B S is a persistent disk, an instance store is a temporary disk, E F S shares files between Linux servers, and F S x gives Windows file shares and more. S three Standard is for frequent use, Standard I A for infrequent use, and Glacier for archives. Multi-A Z gives failover, and a read replica gives read scaling. R D S is a managed relational database, Aurora is compatible with My S Q L and Postgres, DynamoDB is key-value, and ElastiCache is an in-memory cache. Storage Gateway reaches on-premises data, Backup makes policy-based copies, and Elastic Disaster Recovery gives fast recovery. Exam tip: ask what the data model is, and how much you want to manage.

1.title: Look-Alikes: Networking, Integration, AI and Analytics
1.text: Now networking, integration, A I and analytics. A V P N is encrypted over the internet, and Direct Connect is a dedicated line. Route fifty-three is D N S, CloudFront caches content at the edge, and Global Accelerator gives static addresses and routes traffic over the A W S network. S Q S is a queue, S N S fans a message out, EventBridge handles events and schedules, and Step Functions runs workflows. Comprehend finds insights in text, Textract reads scanned forms, Transcribe turns speech into text, and Polly turns text into speech. Rekognition analyzes images, Lex builds chatbots, and SageMaker A I is for your own models. Athena runs S Q L on S three, Redshift is the data warehouse, E M R runs Hadoop and Spark, and OpenSearch handles search and logs. Kinesis handles streams, Firehose delivers them, and Glue prepares and catalogs data. Exam tip: pre-built A I services do one task, while SageMaker A I is for your own models.

1.title: Look-Alikes: Billing, Pricing and Support
1.text: Now billing, pricing and support. Savings Plans commit you to an hourly spend, and Reserved Instances commit you to a configuration. Spot is interruptible, Dedicated Hosts suit your own licenses, and Capacity Reservations guarantee capacity. The Pricing Calculator estimates, Cost Explorer analyzes, and Budgets warns. Tags label your costs, and Cost and Usage Reports give the detailed data. Compute Optimizer rightsizes, and Trusted Advisor runs checks and gives recommendations. Basic Support is for everyone, Business Support plus is for production, Enterprise Support adds a T A M, and Unified Operations is the fastest response. The Health Dashboard shows A W S problems that affect you, while Trusted Advisor checks your own account. Professional Services is A W S consulting, Partners are the ecosystem, and Marketplace is software you can buy. Exam tip: cost questions hide in plain sight, so look for the words estimate, analyze, warn and commit.

1.title: Service Chooser: Security, Identity and Governance
1.text: Now the service chooser, which starts from the need. I need to give an application temporary access: use an I A M role. I need to protect the root user: use M F A, create no access keys, and do not use it every day. I need to find A W S's compliance reports: use A W S Artifact. I need to record who changed a setting: use A W S CloudTrail. I need to block S Q L injection at a load balancer: use A W S W A F. I need to detect stolen credentials: use Amazon GuardDuty. I need to scan servers for vulnerabilities: use Amazon Inspector. I need to encrypt data and manage the keys: use A W S K M S. And I need to set up many accounts with guardrails: use A W S Control Tower. Exam tip: name the verb in the need: record, block, detect, scan, encrypt.

1.title: Service Chooser: Compute, Storage, Databases and Networking
1.text: The second chooser covers compute, storage, databases and networking. I need to run a server I control: use Amazon E C two. I need to add and remove servers with demand: use E C two Auto Scaling. I need to run containers with no servers, or code on an event: use Fargate, or Lambda. I need to archive for years at the lowest cost: use S three Glacier Deep Archive. I need to share files between Linux servers: use Amazon E F S. I need a managed relational database: use Amazon R D S. I need millisecond key lookups at any scale: use Amazon DynamoDB. I need to deliver content faster worldwide: use Amazon CloudFront. And I need a dedicated line to my data center: use A W S Direct Connect. Exam tip: match the data model, and the management you want, to the service.

1.title: Service Chooser: AI, Analytics, Integration, Cost and Support
1.text: The third chooser covers A I, analytics, integration, cost and support. I need to find the sentiment of reviews: use Amazon Comprehend. I need to pull text out of scanned invoices: use Amazon Textract. I need to run S Q L on files in S three: use Amazon Athena. I need to send one message to many receivers: use Amazon S N S. I need to estimate a cost before building: use the A W S Pricing Calculator. I need a warning before spending passes a limit: use A W S Budgets. I need to save on steady usage, or on interruptible work: use Savings Plans, or Spot. I need cloud engineers around the clock for production: use Business Support plus. And I need to buy third-party software: use A W S Marketplace. Exam tip: if two answers fit, choose the one that needs less setup or grants less access.

1.title: Lists the Exam Likes
1.text: These are the lists the exam likes, and they are easy points. The six advantages of cloud computing: variable expense, economies of scale, no capacity guessing, speed and agility, no data center upkeep, and a global reach in minutes. The six pillars: operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization and sustainability. The seven Rs: retire, retain, rehost, relocate, replatform, repurchase and refactor. The S three storage classes: Standard, Intelligent-Tiering, Standard I A, One Zone I A, Glacier Instant Retrieval, Glacier Flexible Retrieval and Glacier Deep Archive. The E C two purchasing options: On-Demand, Savings Plans, Reserved Instances, Spot, Dedicated Hosts, Dedicated Instances and Capacity Reservations. And the support plans: Basic, Business Support plus, Enterprise Support and Unified Operations. Exam tip: say each list aloud from memory.

1.title: Terms That Trip People Up
1.text: Here are the terms that trip people up. A Region is a group of Availability Zones. An Availability Zone is one or more data centers with separate power. An edge location is a cache near your users. Elasticity means capacity follows demand, and high availability means the workload survives a failure. Least privilege means only the permissions a task needs. Stateful means replies are allowed automatically, and stateless means replies need their own rule. Serverless means no servers to provision or manage. To decouple is to connect parts through a queue or events. Tiered pricing means the price per unit falls as volume rises. And consolidated billing gives one bill, shared discounts and many accounts. Exam tip: when two terms look alike, say the one-line difference before you answer.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. On one page, the exam has four domains, sixty-five questions, ninety minutes, and a pass mark of seven hundred. For look-alikes, learn the one-line job of each service, because the exam describes the job. For the chooser, name the verb in the need, and then the service. For lists, know the six advantages, the six pillars, the seven Rs, the S three classes, the E C two options and the support plans. And for terms, know Region, zone, edge, elasticity, stateful, serverless, decouple and tiered pricing. Next, Module sixteen covers exam technique and a final review.
